Resolve prey to the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy (key, exact name, then fuzzy)

Source: R/dv_taxonomy_gbif.R
dv_taxonomy_gbif.Rd

The terrestrial and freshwater counterpart of dv_taxonomy_worms(): matches each unique prey to the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy, which covers all kingdoms, and returns its lineage for the declared ranks. It follows the same rules and returns the same provenance columns, so dv_prepare(), dv_taxonomy_report() and the rest of the package treat both sources alike. Matching proceeds in this order:

  1. id - a GBIF taxon key is already known (prey_id). Its record is read: a synonym is followed to its accepted taxon ("id_synonym") and the prey name stored with it is compared with the GBIF name (name_check). If the record cannot be read, the key is left unresolved for now ("id_unchecked", lineage_ok = FALSE). A key GBIF does not know falls back to the prey name ("id_fallback_name");

  2. exact - the GBIF species-match service finds the name as written;

  3. fuzzy - (if fuzzy = TRUE) the service proposes a close name, which can rescue a misspelling;

  4. higherrank - the name itself is unknown but a coarser taxon in it is (e.g. the genus of an unknown species); the lineage stops at that rank, so the record shows as unidentified below it. A step up to a kingdom alone (what GBIF answers for "Plastic" with kingdom = "Animalia") is treated as no match;

  5. unresolved - nothing matched; all ranks stay NA.

A name can belong to several taxa (Polychaeta is a class of worms and a genus of flies). GBIF then steps up to their shared ancestor, or gives no match. DietView looks at the alternatives GBIF lists: when exactly one of them is an exact match to an accepted name (in kingdom, if given), it is taken; when several are, the conservative GBIF answer is kept and the prey is flagged as a possible homonym, to be settled by a lineage table. A name matched as a synonym gets the classification of its accepted taxon. Every match type other than "id" and "exact", a name that differs from the GBIF name, a match below min_confidence and a possible homonym are listed by dv_taxonomy_report() for review.

Usage

dv_taxonomy_gbif(
  keys,
  ranks = c("kingdom", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "species"),
  cache_dir = tools::R_user_dir("DietView", "cache"),
  fuzzy = TRUE,
  kingdom = NULL,
  min_confidence = 90,
  cache_max_age = 180,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

keys

Data.frame with columns prey_id (GBIF taxon key, may be NA) and prey_name (may be NA); one row per unique prey. Other columns are kept.

ranks

Ranks to keep (default the seven flagship ranks). GBIF returns kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus and species; any other rank stays NA.

cache_dir

Directory for the on-disk cache. NULL disables caching.

fuzzy

If TRUE (default), accept fuzzy matches. FALSE asks GBIF for strict matching only.

kingdom

Optional kingdom hint passed to GBIF (e.g. "Animalia"), which helps with names shared by a plant and an animal genus.

min_confidence

GBIF confidence (0-100) below which a match is listed for review (default 90). The match is kept.

cache_max_age

Maximum age, in days, of a cached lookup (default 180).

verbose

Print progress.

Value

keys with one column per rank plus gbif_key, match_type ("id", "id_synonym", "id_unchecked", "id_fallback_name", "exact", "fuzzy", "higherrank", "unresolved"), name_check, matched_name, confidence, n_candidates (exact-name candidates GBIF listed), homonym, lineage_ok, retrieved and low_confidence.

Details

The GBIF Backbone has no class for some groups (ray-finned fishes, for instance, sit directly under Chordata). With dv_prepare(gaps = "label"), the default, such a missing rank is filled as "Chordata (no class)" instead of looking unidentified.

Needs internet access to api.gbif.org and no extra package. Successful lookups are cached to disk, in their own file next to the WoRMS cache, with the same expiry rules (cache_max_age); failed lookups are never cached and are retried on the next run, getOption("DietView.gbif_retries", 3) times per request with a 1, 2, 4 ... second backoff.

See also

dv_taxonomy_worms() for marine prey; dv_parse_lineage() when the lineage already comes with the data (e.g. from a metabarcoding pipeline).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# needs internet access
keys <- data.frame(prey_id   = c(NA, 8084280),
                   prey_name = c("Crangon vulgaris", "Gadus morhua"))
dv_taxonomy_gbif(keys)
} # }
